taxonomy:
Here's a taxonomy of the grid-based logic games from the provided information, categorized by their core mechanics:

**I. Placement Puzzles**
    *   **Light Placement:**
        *   Akari (Place light bulbs, illuminate white squares, bulbs don't illuminate each other)
    *   **Number/Symbol Placement:**
        *   Chained Block (Fill cells, consecutive black cells form "blocks" with numbered counts, blocks form "chains")
        *   Choco Banana (Fill cells based on block sizes and chain formations)
        *   Fillomino (Divide into blocks of five cells, numbers indicate surrounding lines)
        *   Nansuke (Fill blank cells with numbers from a list, numbers are directional)
        *   Nurikabe (Color cells black, numbers indicate white cell count to nearest black cell/frame, white cells form continuous network, black cells don't touch)
        *   Nuritwin (Shade cells, regions contain two blocks of same size, numbers indicate block size)
        *   Sto-stone (Fill colored cells, numbers in "rooms" indicate continuous black cells, black cells don't connect across rooms, stones "drop" to fill bottom half)
        *   Sudoku (Place 1-9 in empty cells, no repeats in rows, columns, or 3x3 blocks)
        *   Usowan (Fill colored cells, numbers in diagonal cells indicate black cells to right/down)
    *   **Shape/Object Placement:**
        *   Evolomino (Divide into blocks, blocks contain pairs of same-shaped white/gray areas, numbers indicate half the block's cell count)
        *   Five Cells (Draw squares in white cells, squares form "blocks", arrows pass through blocks)
        *   LITS (Color four consecutive squares (tetrominoes) in designated areas, same shapes can't touch, colored squares form connected network)
        *   Shakashaka (Place black "triangles in squares", numbers indicate surrounding black triangles, remaining white areas form rectangles/squares)

**II. Path/Loop Puzzles**
    *   **Line Drawing (Single Loop):**
        *   Dotchi-Loop (Draw lines through cell centers to make a single loop, loop goes through white circles, avoids black circles)
        *   Masyu (Draw lines through cell centers to make a single loop, loop through all circles, white circles straight, black circles turn then straight)
        *   Nagareru (Draw a single continuous loop in a direction, loop through arrow cells, wind affects movement)
        *   Pencils (Draw lines from pencil tips, lines through cells, numbers show pencil length, lines don't cross/branch)
        *   Slitherlink (Connect adjacent dots with lines to make a single loop, numbers indicate surrounding lines)
        *   Suraromu (Make a single loop through cell centers, loop passes "Gates" between black cells/frame, number in circle indicates gates to pass)
        *   Yajilin (Draw a single loop, loop through cell centers, numbers indicate black cells in arrow direction, loop avoids black cells/numbers, black cells don't touch)
    *   **Line Drawing (Multiple Paths/Connections):**
        *   Numberlink (Connect pairs of same numbers with a continuous line, lines through cell centers, avoid numbers, no crossing/branching)
    *   **Loop with Room Constraints:**
        *   Moon-or-Sun (Draw a single loop through cell centers, loop through all moon or sun cells in a room, each room entered once, alternating moon/sun focus between rooms)
        *   Hashiwokakero (Connect islands with bridges, number indicates bridges per island, max two bridges between islands, bridges don't cross)

**III. Coloring/Painting Puzzles**
    *   **Area Coloring with Constraints:**
        *   Hebi (Place numbers 1-5 in squares to form snakes, snakes don't touch, directional rules for snake interaction)
        *   Heyawake (Color cells, numbers in "rooms" indicate painted cells, white cells not cut off/form loops, painted cells don't connect)
        *   Nurimeizu (Paint cells to create a maze from S to G, "Rooms" are all painted or all white, white cells not cut off/form loops, S/G/circle/triangle rooms not painted)
        *   Nurimisaki (Fill cells, circles are "Misaki" (Promontory) and remain white, non-circle cells can be black, Misaki cells have one white neighbor, numbers indicate straight line of white cells)
        *   Tilepaint (Color "tiles" based on rules, numbers in diagonal cells indicate black cells to right/down)

**IV. Movement/Transformation Puzzles**
    *   **Object Movement:**
        *   Satogaeri (Move circles horizontally/vertically in "Countries", each country one circle, numbers indicate cells to pass through)
        *   Yosenabe (Move circles vertically/horizontally into gray areas, arrows show movement, numbers in gray areas equal sum of entering circles)

**V. Grid Division Puzzles**
    *   **Block Formation:**
        *   Makaro (Divide grid into L-shaped blocks, blocks one cell wide, open circles are knee of block, arrows point to knee, numbers indicate block size)
        *   Sashigane (Divide grid into L-shaped blocks, one block wide, open circles are knee of block, arrows point to knee)

**VI. Other/Combined Mechanics**
    *   **Grid Transformation/Analysis:**
        *   Double Choco (Divide grid into blocks, blocks have same-shaped white/gray areas, numbers indicate half block's cell count)
        *   Hitori (Color cells, no number repeats in row/column, black cells' sides don't touch, white cells form continuous network)
        *   Juosan (Fill cells with '-' or '|' marks, numbers in "Territories" indicate mark count, mark extension rules)
        *   Kurodoko (Color cells black, numbers indicate white cell count to nearest black cell/frame, cells with numbers are white, black cells don't touch, white cells connected)
        *   Kurotto (Fill/color cells, numbers in circles sum of continuous black cells vertically/horizontally, cells with circles not colored)
        *   Mid-loop (Fill cells with numbers in "Rooms", rooms contain numbers 1 to cell count, numbers in black cells with arrows indicate max surrounding number, number not adjacent to same number in another room)
        *   Shikaku (Numbers indicate surrounding black triangles, remaining white areas form rectangles/squares)
    *   **Directional/Arrow Puzzles:**
        *   Yajilin (Draw a single loop, loop through cell centers, numbers indicate black cells in arrow direction, loop avoids black cells/numbers, black cells don't touch)
